question: The sides of a triangle are 37 cm, 44 cm and 15 cm. What is the length of its altitude corresponding to the side with the length of 44 cm?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Semi-perimeter (s) = (37 + 44 + 15) ÷ 2 = 48 cm.

Area using Heron's formula = √[48 × 11 × 4 × 33] = 264 cm².

Altitude on the 44 cm side = (2 × Area) ÷ Base = (2 × 264) ÷ 44 = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The sides of the triangle are a = 37 cm, b = 44 cm, and c = 15 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Semi-perimeter, s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

Area of triangle = √[s × (s − a) × (s − b) × (s − c)]

Area = 1/2 × base × height

 
 
 
 
 
 
 44 cm 15 cm 37 cm h = ? A B C D 

**Calculations:**

⇒ s = (37 + 44 + 15) ÷ 2 = 96 ÷ 2 = 48 cm.

⇒ Area = √[48 × (48 − 37) × (48 − 44) × (48 − 15)]

⇒ Area = √[48 × 11 × 4 × 33]

⇒ Area = √[(16 × 3) × 11 × 4 × (3 × 11)]

⇒ Area = √[64 × 9 × 121]

⇒ Area = 8 × 3 × 11 = 264 cm².

Now, substitute the calculated area and the given base (44 cm) into the altitude formula:

⇒ 264 = 1/2 × 44 × h

⇒ 264 = 22 × h

⇒ h = 264 ÷ 22

⇒ h = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

It is universally used to calculate the area of any triangle when the lengths of all three sides are known, without needing any altitude or angle. The formula is Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)].

Altitudes of a Triangle

An altitude is a perpendicular line segment drawn from a vertex to the opposite side (or its extension). Every triangle has exactly three altitudes, which intersect at a single distinct point called the orthocenter.

Relation between Area and Altitude

Once the area is known, the altitude corresponding to any given base can be easily found using the standard formula: Area = 1/2 × base × height. It is notable that the shortest altitude of a triangle always corresponds to its longest side.
